title: Exposure hallway handoff protocols (canary + AB) - WIP
content:
Purpose
---
Quick working doc to capture a compact, reproducible 'hallway handoff' protocol for canaries and small A/B experiments. This is intentionally lightweight — intended to run on top of the existing rollout playbooks, but focused on the human handoffs between product, SRE, and the owning eng team during the first 6–48 hours of exposure.

Scope / what this is NOT
- Focus: cross-functional comms, ceremony, immediate telemetry checks, quick rollback/fallback triggers, and who does what in the hallway.
- Not a replacement for the full Experiment Runbook or SRE runbooks (link above).
- Not covering long-running A/B analysis (stats engine work), only operational exposure phase.

Quick glossary
- Exposure window: first 6–48 hours after any non-zero traffic is sent to a new variant/canary.
- Hallway handoff: synchronous or near-synchronous check-in (Slack call / Zoom) with product + eng + SRE + CS on initial traffic day.
- Safety net: automated and manual mechanisms to stop exposure and re-route to stable variants.

High-level principles (short)
1) Triage fast, escalate faster: if a guardrail trips, we prefer immediate mitigation over investigating root cause.
2) Single source of truth for 'exposure state' in the ticket (ticket status + rollout tag).
3) Keep the customer-facing surface protected: if any downstream reliability or safety metric degrades, bias to reduce/exclude external traffic first.

Pre-launch checklist (pre-hallway) — owning eng + product (do before exposure)
- Confirm experiment metadata in ticket: hypothesis, target cohort, % exposure, start time, stop time, primary metric(s), safety metrics.
- Confirm model pinned version(s) and fallback mapping (which variant to route if canary fails).
- Confirm monitoring dashboard links and alert thresholds (list dashboards in ticket).
- Confirm oncall roster for first 48 hours: primary eng, backup eng, SRE, product owner, CS lead.
- Confirm comms channel: #rollouts/<short-name> and a pinned thread created 15m before start.
- Canary cohort examples: internal-only, employees-only, 0.1% telecom sample, region-limited, or feature-flag gate. Choose the simplest that covers the hypothesis.
- Smoke test plan: 8–10 quick prompts/requests that exercise common failure modes (latency spikes, malformed output, hallucination patterns, rate limit edge). Put list in ticket.

Hallway handoff choreography (T=0 to T+1h)
- T-minus 15m: product pings channel, confirms 'green' from SRE + eng for GO.
- T=0: owner flips exposure to X% (or opens flag). Post: "exposure started — X% to variant B. smoke tests running."
- T+5m: owner runs smoke list, posts results (pass/fail and sample outputs).
- T+15m: SRE posts initial system-level digest (p50/p95 latency, error rate, infra load).
- T+30m: product posts initial quality signal (sample quality scoring from eval hooks or quick human spot-check).
- T+60m: synced 10–15m hallway stand (Slack huddle or short Zoom) to confirm go/no-go to continue ramp. Agenda below.

Minute-by-minute hallway agenda (T+60m stand)
- Quick readouts (each 1–2 min): eng (errors/latency), SRE (infra), product (quality), CS (customer noise), data/metrics (early statistical flags).
- Decision ask: continue ramp / hold / roll back. Decision owner = Product with SRE concurrence.
- If decision = continue, agree on next checkpoint time (usually +2h). If hold, immediate actions listed in ticket.

Operational gating rules (practical knobs)
- Auto-trips (immediate stop): total 5xx rate > X% sustained for 3m; queue depth > threshold; GPU OOMs; deployment panics.
- Quality safety (manual stop suggested): automated toxicity or hallucination classifier false-positive > threshold OR a steady drop in 'coherence' quality metric > relative delta. These require product + eng signoff to continue.
- Latency budget breach: if p95 latency > SLO * 2 for > 5m, SRE to throttle exposure or enable fallback pool.

Ticket update pattern (single source of truth)
- Title: [EXPOSURE] <feature> v<ver> — <X%> — yyyy-mm-dd hh:mmZ
- Top pinned section: current state (started / paused / rolled back), last decision time, responsible owners.
- Timeline section: timestamped short notes for each checkpoint + decisions + sample outputs.
- Links: dashboards, smoke tests, experiment dataset, revert PR link if any.

Sample Slack messages (templates)
- Start: "[EXPOSURE] STARTED — <feature> vX — 0.5% traffic -> variant B. Smoke tests running. Owner: @asha. Channel: #rollouts/feature-x"
- Smoke pass: "[EXPOSURE] SMOKE PASS @ T+5m — no 5xx, latency nominal, sample outputs: <link>"
- Hold: "[EXPOSURE] HOLD — observed sustained p95 latency > target for 7m. @sre-team reducing exposure to 0.05% while investigating. Decision owner: @product. Next checkpoint in 1h."
- Rollback: "[EXPOSURE] ROLLBACK — rolling back to default model. Reason: elevated error rate and external customer reports. See ticket JIRA-OPS-1897 for details."

Escalation matrix (if hallway can't resolve)
- Level 1: owning eng + SRE — try immediate mitigation (single config change, traffic reduction). 0–30m.
- Level 2: oncall lead + product + infra lead — if not resolved in 30–90m, consider routing to dedicated fallback or rollback.
- Level 3: CTO + SRE manager + customer success director — declare incident, open incident bridge, prepare customer comms. >90m or customer-impacting.

Rollout ramp cadence (example)
- 0% -> 0.1% internal-only (10–60m) -> 0.5% (2–6h) -> 1–5% (day 1) -> stepwise to target over days.
- Keep absolute upper bound for day-0 at 5% unless explicit exec signoff.

A/B experiment notes (operationally different)
- For A/B: keep experiment assignments stable (sticky) for at least 24h for meaningful quality signals. But allow short-lived operational canaries (non-overlapping cohorts) for infra checks.
- If A/B primary metric is quality (not infra), treat initial exposure as conservative: prefer internal/employee sampling + shadow traffic to collect signals.

Fallback options (ordered)
1) Reduce exposure % to minimal safe floor (0.01% or internal-only).
2) Route to previous stable model or to cheaper inference pool.
3) Disable feature flag that triggers variant routing.
4) Full rollback of deployment.

Post-exposure mini-retrospective (T+24–48h)
- Required: short notes in ticket summarizing what tripped, time-to-detect, time-to-mitigate, whether the hypothesis held, and any follow-ups (fix PRs, more checks).
- Optional: invite cross-functional 30m sync if there were surprises (product, eng, SRE, data).

Common failure modes we see (notes to self)
- Telemetry mismatch: signal not tracking (wrong tag) -> prevents early detection. Always validate telemetry tags before start.
- Over-confident auto-escalation thresholds that are too sensitive -> churn. Tune thresholds by traffic pattern.
- Human bottleneck: if single person is gate, they become a blocker. Always have backup.

Quick decision rubric (one-liner)
- Safety-critical metric breached -> STOP.
- Customer-reported degradation -> STOP, unless isolated to small cohort.
- Only minor/noisy metric fluctuation -> HOLD or slow ramp.

Open questions / TODOs (short)
- Should we make a small "handshake" API for automating the ticket state (start/hold/rollback) so we can reduce manual Slack posts? (tech spike?)
- Which library do we standardize for 'smoke test packs'? (small repo exists, need owner).
- How to better integrate short A/B sticky assignment with our canary gating without blowing up analysis downstream?

Appendix: quick smoke list template (copy into ticket)
- 10 typical prompt/requests with expected behaviour notes and 1–2 assertions each.
- Latency check: single request p50/p95, concurrent (10x) p50/p95.
- Error check: no 5xx in 5m window.
- Output check: no known hallucination triggers in sample set.

Notes for next iteration
- Convert this sketch into a tiny UI flow in Console for 'Hallway Handoff' that auto-populates the channel, pins smoke tests, and adds checkpoint reminders.
- Add a small checklist that SRE can mark via a tiny API to auto-pause exposure on infra signals.

End — this is intentionally terse and craftable. Use this for the next few canaries and we'll iterate.

Unresolved: add precise numeric thresholds (need SRE + infra data)
